findings.title: The Amazon does not follow the savanna pattern
findings.text: The western Amazon study area stays comparatively green throughout the year. Its raw same-month rain–NDVI association is negative, while the one-month anomaly association is close to zero. These observations do not support a uniform 'more rain, then more greenness' rule across all five regions.

findings.title: What remains after removing the seasons?
findings.text: NDVI's same-month Pearson r is -0.431; comparing rainfall with NDVI one month later gives -0.335. After subtracting each calendar month's usual values, the one-month correlation is -0.030 over 306 paired months. The contrast shows that a large part of the raw association is seasonal, and the delayed anomaly relationship is weak.

findings.title: Cross-check with a second vegetation index
findings.text: EVI's one-month anomaly correlation is -0.038. NDVI and EVI provide complementary greenness measures from the same MODIS product; agreement is useful, but it is not an independent satellite experiment or a measurement of vegetation area. In the rainfall-selected October 2016 example, NDVI changes from 0.827 to 0.832, while EVI falls from 0.561 to 0.548. This disagreement is another reason to avoid presenting every region as a greening success story.
